output.myth: Hilun was a gull who carried messages between the islands and Vel. She flew so close to the Gale that Tavo grew fond of her, and fond is a dangerous thing in a god. One day he laughed and tore the feathers off one wing, the way he tears a sail. Hilun fell into the sea and the Gulls cried for three days. Ennu the Kite-Wright sewed her a wing from old sailcloth and waxed thread, and it did not fly as well as the first, but it flew. When Hesk counted the living at the Reel she found one more than she expected. Hilun had gone up with the cloth wing and hung her spread body on the Windward edge of the sky, where the wind is loudest. Fishermen's wives say that when the gale is about to come, Hilun leans a little, and that is the sign to take the nets in. Tavo still laughs when he passes her, but he goes around.
output.verse:
Gull wing of old cloth,
she leans before the gale's breath,
haul the nets in now.
